sites.name: Willy T (Wreck)

s1.quote: The Willy T now sits just off of Key Bay at Peter Island. The wreck lies in 65 ft of water with the crow’s nest at 35 ft.

s2.quote: The wreck of the Willy T lies on a sandy seabed at a maximum depth of around 67 feet (20.5 meters), while her masts extend upwards to a depth of approximately 38 feet (11.5 meters).

highlights.text: Replica pirates and cannons; on-deck bar to visit

summary.text: A former floating bar sunk in 2019 off Peter Island as an artificial reef. Its masts reach roughly 35-38 ft, the hull rests on sand near 65 ft, and divers can enter the decorated wreck.

sites.depthNote: Moved from Norman Island; now in Key Bay, Peter Island

s1.quote: The beautiful Kodiak Queen sits in a maximum depth of 57ft off the shore of Virgin Gorda

s2.quote: The top of the wire Kraken lies 20-feet (6.1 m) below the surface and the ship sits on the sandy seabed at 55-feet (16.8 m).

highlights.text: Wire Kraken sculpture on a former Pearl Harbor survivor

summary.text: The former Navy fuel barge Kodiak Queen was sunk in 2017 off Virgin Gorda as an art reef topped by a wire Kraken sculpture. It rests in about 55-57 ft, with open-water divers exploring the outside and penetration left to advanced divers.
